stem: During a procedure planned for moderate sedation, the client stops responding purposefully to verbal or light tactile stimulation and develops airway obstruction. Which nursing response is most appropriate?

options.A: Continue the planned sedation because loss of purposeful response is expected during moderate sedation
options.B: Recognize deeper-than-intended sedation, initiate airway rescue measures within the nurse's training/protocol, and summon qualified assistance immediately
options.C: Wait for spontaneous recovery because intervening with the airway can deepen the level of sedation
options.D: Increase the sedative dose to reduce agitation during airway obstruction before calling for assistance

rationale: Moderate sedation is intended to preserve purposeful response to verbal commands or light tactile stimulation. A client who no longer responds purposefully and develops airway obstruction has progressed beyond the intended level and requires rescue. ASA guidance emphasizes training in airway maintenance, management of sedation-related complications, and rescue from deeper-than-intended sedation. The nurse should stop treating the situation as routine moderate sedation, support the airway according to training and facility protocol, and summon qualified help.
educational_objective: A client who loses purposeful responsiveness and develops airway compromise during intended moderate sedation requires immediate recognition of deeper-than-intended sedation and airway rescue with qualified assistance.
source_document_title: Statement on Sedation & Anesthesia Administration in Dental Office-Based Settings
source_locator: Training & Education — airway maintenance; management of airway compromise/hemodynamic instability; rescue from deeper than intended level of sedation
source_claim_supported: ASA explicitly requires training in airway maintenance and rescue from deeper-than-intended sedation; ASA sedation definitions describe moderate sedation as maintaining purposeful response to verbal or light tactile stimulation.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — Therapeutic Procedures, printed p. 44 (PDF page 47): manage client during a procedure with moderate sedation; manage client following a procedure with moderate sedation
blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — moderate sedation monitoring and rescue
correction_summary: Converted competency trivia into a deterioration/rescue scenario, corrected the blueprint to Reduction of Risk Potential, and framed the nursing action within training and facility protocol to avoid scope overreach.

audit_findings.source_audit: Official ASA statement verified; NCSBN 2026 moderate-sedation activity statement verified.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: Purposeful-response distinction, airway-compromise concern and rescue training are directly supported.
audit_findings.choice_A: Incorrect; loss of purposeful response plus obstruction is not routine moderate sedation.
audit_findings.choice_B: Correct; identifies deeper sedation and immediate rescue/escalation.
audit_findings.choice_C: Unsafe delay in an airway emergency.
audit_findings.choice_D: Unsafe; additional sedative can worsen respiratory compromise.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B combines correct recognition and safe response.
